competition.contract: Integer-ps reconstruction from full ordinary events. Context clocks partition into service, missing consumable contiguous operand, and ready but another shared grant. Pre-start capacity counts use half-open occupancy intervals and clock edges; same-tick ordering/alignment remains in the residual. Fetch-full waiting uses wall-time intersections because allocation need not be clock-aligned. Dependency-to-allocation may also include SRAM/cache/tag availability. Input/scale waits overlap. The last-descriptor split partitions observed operand waiting; it does not isolate a native latency. Outstanding/MC-full intersections are observed window occupancy and can overlap; they do not prove every missed issue opportunity or a uniquely responsible resource. Overlapping per-task/context counters are not additive wall-clock stalls or removable latency. The latest-finishing dependency chain omits implicit shared-resource edges; no global causal attribution.
